title: Turning verbs into nouns
description: Say what a thing is, and what it is for.

explanation.summary: Spanish turns verbs into nouns with endings, and the endings follow a pattern. It is a very productive way to write, and it is everywhere in formal Spanish.

sections.heading: The four endings
sections.body: An -ar verb makes a noun ending in -ción: hablar becomes la comunicación, or a noun ending in -amiento: emplear becomes el empleo. An -er or -ir verb makes -ción: comer becomes la reunión, or -imiento: vivir becomes el movimiento. The -ción nouns are always feminine, and the -amiento and -imiento nouns are usually masculine.

examples.es: La reunión empieza a las nueve.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: The noun often takes a preposition that the verb did not: decidir takes en, and la decisión takes sobre or de. Cambiar takes por and el cambio takes de. So the noun is not only a new word, it comes with its own grammar.

examples.es: La decisión sobre el presupuesto fue difícil.
examples.en: The decision about the budget was difficult.

examples.es: El cambio de idioma no fue fácil.
examples.en: The change of language was not easy.

examples.es: La satisfacción del cliente es lo primero.

exercises.note: A verb can become a noun: hablar becomes la hablar, el hablar; llegar becomes la llegada.
